problem:
$$
⟨f(x),g(x)⟩={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }f(x)g(x)\,\text{d}x
$$

Given the inner product on the set of continuous functions over $x\in [-\pi ,\pi ]$ defined above, select the correct options below.$\,$
$⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x),1⟩=$ 
{{field-1}}

$\,$
The functions $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)$ and $g(x)=1$ 
{{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
Evaluating the inner product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x),1⟩ & ={\int }_{-\pi }^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{1}{6}\operatorname{cos}⁡(6x)]}_{-\pi }^{\pi } \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(6\pi )-\operatorname{cos}⁡(-6\pi )) \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}(1-1) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡(6x)$ and $g(x)=1$ $\text{are orthogonal}$ with respect to the inner product.
